purpose: Record the article's 63 Cagayan River eel samples and a GenBank accession crosswalk while distinguishing source taxon labels, database annotations, collection dates, and unresolved reuse and taxonomic decisions.

source.title: Identification of Tropical Freshwater Eels, Anguilla spp., in Cagayan River, Philippines
source.provider: The Philippine Agricultural Scientist, University of the Philippines Los Baños College of Agriculture and Food Science
source.citation: Hilario, J. A., Choresca, C. H. Jr., Danting, M. J. C., Magbanua, F. L. T., & Oclos, M. T. T. (2022). Identification of Tropical Freshwater Eels, Anguilla spp., in Cagayan River, Philippines. The Philippine Agricultural Scientist, 105(3), 226–235. https://doi.org/10.62550/ABC001021
source.fullTextAccess: The official UPLB/PAS abstract page was reviewed. Full text was reviewed in an author-uploaded ResearchGate copy attributed to Joyce Hilario; the official linked PDF endpoint was not retrievable during review. ResearchGate labels the content as potentially subject to copyright.
source.license: No item-specific open license or reuse permission was verified. Public access to the author-uploaded copy and public GenBank accessions are not treated as permission to reproduce the article, figures, or tables.

study.waterbody: Cagayan River; source text names Barangay Toran, Aparri, Cagayan as the collection locality.
study.sourceReportedCollectionProcess: The paper says 63 eels (23 glass eels, 20 elvers, 20 yellow eels) were randomly sampled at the BFAR National Freshwater Fisheries Technology Center eel culture facility. It then says the specimens were collected from the Cagayan River at Barangay Toran, Aparri, and transported to the facility. The paper does not give field collection dates, coordinates, station-level effort, or a capture boundary.
study.identificationMethod: Morphological assessment by life stage followed by mitochondrial cytochrome-b sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. The article itself reports morphology/genetics discrepancies, including overlap or misidentification among A. marmorata and A. luzonensis.

genbankAccessionCrosswalk.articleTaxonLabel: Anguilla bicolor pacifica (molecular result); A. bicolor in morphology section

genbankQualifierAudit.interpretation: GenBank provides collection_date values grouped by the sample isolate labels and linked accessions. The article itself does not state field sampling dates. Absence of country/coordinate/voucher qualifiers in these records does not negate the paper's named source locality and does not establish a surveyed location or physical voucher.

taxonomicConceptReview.catalogOfFishesCurrentStatus: The Eschmeyer Catalog of Fishes record updated 13 August 2026 lists Anguilla pacifica as valid and documents differing historical/subspecies treatments.
taxonomicConceptReview.wormsCurrentStatus: WoRMS lists Anguilla bicolor pacifica as unaccepted and accepts Anguilla bicolor.
taxonomicConceptReview.ncbiTaxonomyStatus: The NCBI Taxonomy record uses Anguilla pacifica as current name and Anguilla bicolor pacifica as a homotypic synonym, while explicitly warning that NCBI Taxonomy is not an authoritative nomenclature source.
taxonomicConceptReview.decision: Retain the article label and GenBank organism annotation as separate source assertions. Do not collapse either to a single Bangwit taxon or occurrence until the project selects a taxonomic authority and records the applied taxon concept.

evidenceLimits: This is a small historical eel harvest/sample with 63 specimens across three life stages, not a standardized survey of the Cagayan basin, tributaries, or multiple stations.
The article names Barangay Toran, Aparri as source locality but gives no coordinates, station, sampling effort, or exact capture geometry; GenBank accessions have no latitude/longitude qualifiers.
The article does not state field collection dates. The three dates recorded by GenBank are retained as accession-linked qualifiers, not independently corroborated article dates.
The article and taxonomic databases use conflicting accepted-name concepts for the shortfin-eel lineage. Source taxon labels must not be silently harmonized.
GenBank sequence accessions are molecular records, not physical specimen voucher/catalog identifiers; no specimen_voucher qualifiers were present in the 63-record query.
The article warns that morphology alone can misidentify Anguilla species, especially where A. marmorata and A. luzonensis characteristics overlap.
No article-specific reuse license was verified; neither the author-uploaded copy nor the public sequence records authorize republication of the article, tables, or figures.
This historical study does not establish current presence, abundance, diet, catchability, fishing permission, safety, legal season, or basin-wide distribution.
No species or occurrence rows, public geometry, tables, figures, or app content were added from this review.

relationshipToOtherSources.yoshinagaEtAl2014: A separate 2009 estuary glass-eel study at Aparri with two dated collections; its sample counts and source-attributed identifications must not be merged with Hilario et al.'s 2018 accession dates or 63 eels.
relationshipToOtherSources.aoyamaEtAl2015: A separate monthly estuary recruitment study with different sampling periods and denominator; do not pool counts or treat either paper as a freshwater-basin checklist.
relationshipToOtherSources.cascoEtAl2025: A 2023 Toran fyke-net landing-site bycatch study. Its landing location and catch sample are a distinct evidence stream; do not merge with this study's 2018 accessioned eel samples.
relationshipToOtherSources.watanabeEtAl2009: The Cagayan-system description of A. luzonensis is an independent taxonomic/locality source, not a substitute for accession-level evidence or Hilario et al.'s sample context.

nextAction: Continue Region II discovery with independently accessible, site-linked river, lake, reservoir, wetland, estuary, and brackish fish sources. For this study, keep the newly reviewed 2018 GenBank dates and sample accessions as research evidence; do not infer field dates, coordinates, or a basin-wide eel inventory.
